catalysts.headline: Microvast reported Q3 2026 results after market close: revenue $45.8M, down 62.8% YoY from $123.3M, missing consensus of ~$74.2M; volume fell ~62% to 190 MWh on weaker heavy-duty truck, port equipment and mining equipment demand in Europe/APAC plus industry pricing pressure; gross margin collapsed to 5.2% from 37.6% a year earlier (incl. a $9.3M inventory write-down); GAAP net loss $76.8M (vs -$1.5M a year earlier), including a $35.7M long-lived-asset impairment; non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA -$60.8M (vs +$21.9M a year earlier); cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash of $124.4M as of 2026-09-30 versus $196M of debt obligations maturing within 12 months; company disclosed substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern and said it has 'limited visibility' into revenue for the next several quarters, and has stopped reporting its order backlog
catalysts.impact: Stock fell sharply the following session(s) — reported premarket move of approximately -48.5% on 2026-11-11, and the -64.3% session move on file for 2026-11-10/11 is consistent in direction with this print; exact percentage not independently re-confirmed against a live quote this pass

Reverse-split check (per task instruction, given the size of the -64.3% move): no reverse-split announcement, record date, or ratio was found in any source searched. A Trendlyne corporate-actions page explicitly states Microvast has not split its stock since 2000 (checked as of Aug 2026). Multiple independent, mutually consistent price readings ($0.22 Benzinga Nov 10; $0.22 MEXC Nov 14) bracket the move and are NOT split-adjusted-looking figures (no round-number jump consistent with a 1-for-N ratio). Conclusion: this move is treated as a genuine price crash tied to the Q3 2026 earnings miss and going-concern disclosure, not a reverse split — flagged here per task instruction since the possibility was explicitly investigated and ruled out, not confirmed with 100% certainty.
